correctness.rationale: Fourier coefficient convolution gives the exact operator norm as the supremum over lattice-character weight ratios: characters attain each ratio. For >=2 active integer frequencies, their lengths >=1 and the radial majorant (1+(sum r_i)^2)/prod(1+r_i²) is strictly decreasing in each r_i because derivative has sign (S-r_i)(1-S r_i)<0. All lengths therefore reduce to 1, giving (1+n²)/2^n, maximized exactly at n=2,3 with 5/4. Equality in triangle inequality forces aligned unit coordinate vectors; s=0 and 0/1 active cases yield 1. Shrinking positive Fourier bumps around m^-1/2 e_1 produce the separate Euclidean lower bound. Independently enumerated short integer tuples; finite enumeration not a universal proof.
residual_risks: Full non-character extremizer structure and exact diagonal-power norm are not established; negative s and other weights excluded.
